HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PAINTED INTRO-CARD, not a class photo, not a cel dump. INTIMATE CLOSE: old Queen Sunduk’s FACE FILLS the left third — match LEFT sheet face exactly (eye shape, grey hair, gold crescent, rust silk). LOW three-quarter, slight dutch. ONE DEVICE: a rust-red #9a3b2a silk ribbon of steam cutting diagonally. Beside her, closer than the others: old Yongsu WHITE hair, one stray white strand, cream-and-blue silk, living BLACK eyes — FOURTH sheet face. Midground bokeh, painted not lined up: Sungman salmon-peach (SECOND) and Chunmyung lavender (THIRD). Foreground dark shoulders: Jesang, Gildal HUMAN rust silk, On Gunhae. Munmu a tiny speck in a warm oval of first light, upper right. Jewel-tone colour: rust, salmon, lavender, cream blooming into the wash; wet-stone catch, paper grain, visible brush. Faces drawn webtoon, world PAINTED. They look toward the mouth, not the lens. One of each. No body halo. No text. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = sunduk, SECOND face = jinduk, THIRD face = chunmyung, FOURTH face = yongsu, FIFTH face = jesang, SIXTH face = gildal, #7 face = ongunhae, #8 face = munmu. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board sunduk (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), binyeo board jinduk (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), crown reference (shape only). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. QUEEN SUNDUK — Look: Pale oval face, dark calm eyes; black hair in a full coiled updo; when crowned, the gold Silla tree-and-antler crown hung with jade gogok. Dress: Crimson court robe with gold phoenix brocade, blue embroidered cape-collar, a red ribbon bow at the chest. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #E8552B. QUEEN JINDUK — Look: As Princess Sungman: a rounder, younger Sacred Bone face than Sunduk, warm dark eyes, a small worried mouth, black hair in a full coiled updo under the gold crescent binyeo. As queen: the same bones, a little thinner, still kind. Dress: Salmon-peach Silla silk jeogori and chima, gold crescent binyeo (attached /ch_seungman.png as princess, /ch_jinduk.png as queen). In the steam cavern: that silk hiked, feet in the water, NO gold crown. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #9d7bd0. PRINCESS CHUNMYUNG — Look: Late forties at her death: a long oval Korean face, dry unhurried eyes, silver-grey in the black hair, a full coiled updo under the gold amethyst binyeo. Young: the same bones, all black hair, sharper mouth (attached /ch_chunmyung_young.png). Dress: Lavender-purple Silla silk jeogori and chima (attached /ch_chunmyung.png). A wax tablet tucked in the sleeve. In the cavern: that silk, feet in the water, NO crown. Colour #d8a0e8. KIM YONGSU — Look: Young (as Bihyung, the madman of Surabol): lean, long loose black hair in a careless topknot with ONE stray strand of hair always poking straight up out of it, exactly as on the attached portrait; thin face, quick crooked half-smile. Now: Old Chief Architect at his death and after: SAME FACE BONES as the attached /ch_yongsu.png, WHITE and grey hair in a crooked topknot with ONE stray WHITE strand still poking straight up, ink on the fingers, cream-and-blue silk a little worn. Talking to a crack or a stream: EYES SOLID WHITE. Looking at Munmu or Chunmyung: living black eyes, sideways total fondness. Colour #6a7cb0. PARK JESANG — Look: Fifties, long grey-white beard and moustache, silver at the temples, a calm half-lidded Korean face, hair in a high topknot. The south-shore Park who can fill a foreign hall. Dress: Magenta-plum silk po over a white inner collar and a dark navy jeogori (attached /ch_park_jesang.png). Bare head, no jougwan, no crown. Hands that have already decided. Colour #8B5A2B. GILDAL — Look: Lean young clerk with a fox mask pushed up on the brow; black hair in a wild topknot, a knowing half-smile, fox-blood streaks painted down the cheeks. Dress: Orange-red wide robe over a magenta inner wrap, white bound forearms, a fox mask riding on the head like a cap. Colour #c45a28. ON GUNHAE — Look: His portrait face: lean like Chunchu and the same height, only a little broader in the jaw and a few years older, with a short trimmed black beard. Never fat, never round-faced. Colour #8a6240. KING MUNMU — Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #C41E3A. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
